marketInsightsHtml:
Le mois de décembre français s'est établi à 176,20 €/MWh et le premier trimestre 2027 à 163,75 €/MWh, tandis que le Day-Ahead français a atteint son plus bas niveau à 60,35 €/MWh après un vent fort et un record de 2,19 GW pour l'éolien offshore français.

L'éolien français passe de 17,4 GW aujourd'hui à 3,3 GW samedi avant de rebondir à 9,0 GW dimanche, tandis que l'éolien allemand passe de 18,4 GW aujourd'hui à 12,7 GW demain et 20,4 GW samedi avant de tomber à environ 6,8-7,4 GW dimanche et lundi, l'éolien néerlandais restant faible entre 0,5 et 1,8 GW.

La disponibilité nucléaire française plus faible d'une année sur l'autre (en moyenne 48,5 GW de novembre à mars) et l'hydroélectricité étanche maintiennent une prime de risque au premier trimestre 27.

marketInsights.gas:
European gas prices are bouncing back slightly this morning after a sharp sell-off yesterday.

TTF front-month is trading up around €82.50/MWh after testing down near €80 support, while NBP December settled at 200.94p/th and NBP Day-Ahead closed at 202.15p/th. Further out, NBP Q1 '27 settled at 197.43p/th, Summer '27 at 150.51p/th, and Winter '27 at 139.78p/th.

The drop was driven by a wider sell-off in stock markets, fund selling, and a roughly 6% fall in carbon prices, which made coal more competitive against gas. More LNG tankers moving through the Strait of Hormuz has also eased competition for cargoes, while talks between Trump, Xi, and Putin in Shenzhen and calmer tanker freight rates have taken some heat out of the market, even with ongoing Gulf tanker strikes and Iranian attacks on US sites in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Weather and supply are pulling in opposite directions. Milder, windier weather for Weeks 47 and 48 and lower cold-snap risks around late November and early December have cooled heating and power-sector gas demand, with Dutch demand dropping from 121.9 mcm to 87.0 mcm as the Dutch system moved from short to long.

On the other hand, a planned 50 mcm/day maintenance outage at Norway's Troll field from today through Saturday brings total offline Norwegian capacity to 88.6 mcm/day. European gas storage is just under 70% full (with the Netherlands at 60.59% and Germany around 57.3%), and SSE has announced plans to close its 311 mcm Atwick storage site from Summer 2027. Brent crude is steady in the low $90s around $92/bbl this morning following US oil and fuel stock builds.
marketInsights.power:
Power curves fell across the board on the back of lower gas, falling carbon prices, and stronger wind forecasts. UK ETS prices saw a sharp drop ahead of Friday's UK–EU summit on emissions linking.

In the UK, December baseload settled at £168.50/MWh and Q1 '27 at £166.10/MWh, while UK N2EX Day-Ahead cleared at £187.88/MWh. On the continent, German December settled at €195.70/MWh and Q1 '27 at €180.60/MWh, with German Day-Ahead jumping to €224.83/MWh on midweek wind dips. French December settled at €176.20/MWh and Q1 '27 at €163.75/MWh, while French Day-Ahead cleared low at €60.35/MWh after strong wind and a 2.19 GW record for French offshore wind.

Wind output is set to drop sharply into the weekend across the main markets, which will increase reliance on gas-fired generation. UK wind is forecast to fall from 7.6 GW today to 4.1 GW tomorrow and 3.0 GW on Saturday, lift to around 8.0 GW on Sunday, and dip back to 3.0 GW on Monday. French wind drops from 17.4 GW today to 3.3 GW on Saturday before bouncing to 9.0 GW on Sunday, while German wind moves from 18.4 GW today to 12.7 GW tomorrow and 20.4 GW on Saturday before falling to around 6.8–7.4 GW on Sunday and Monday, with Dutch wind staying low between 0.5 and 1.8 GW. Temperatures dip into the weekend across the UK (around 4°C on Saturday) and drop to near freezing in Germany and the Netherlands around mid-next week before recovering.

On plant and hydro availability, EDF moved the UK's Torness 2 shutdown into December (22 days offline next month instead of 13), while SSE's 710 MW Medway gas plant is due back on Saturday. Lower year-on-year French nuclear availability (averaging 48.5 GW from November to March) and tight hydro are keeping a risk premium in Q1 '27. Elsewhere, Nordic hydro reserves fell 1.83 TWh to 71% full amid dry Bergen forecasts and Swedish nuclear schedule changes, Spanish hydro rose 330 GWh to 42.9% on heavy rain, and Swiss hydro slipped to a 16.4 percentage point deficit to normal.
